scope: Past Written Papers (PP) series retrieval index. One entry per paper and one per question. This file is an INDEX, not a content source: answer text lives only in the paper spec. Regenerate with build_index.py; never hand-edit.
naming_convention: QP<YY><MM>.html, where QP = Question Paper, YY = year and MM = month of the sitting (QP2607 = July 2026); question_id QP<YY><MM>-Q<n>; anchors #q1..#q9
source_of_truth_policy: specs/<PAPER>.json is authoritative for content. This manifest is authoritative for retrieval. Both index pages and the paper page are generated; editing generated HTML is always wrong.

recurrence_statuses.single: Set once in the sittings MIW has transcribed. NOT "never asked before".
recurrence_statuses.first: Earliest sitting of a family that returns at a later sitting.
recurrence_statuses.repeat_exact: Later sitting; normalised printed stem identical to the first.
recurrence_statuses.repeat_near: Later sitting; printed stem materially reworded.

recurrence_rule: Canonical recurrence is computed chronologically in recurrence_model.py from (year, month) over MIW's own transcriptions, and from nothing else. The source copy host's printed annotation is discovery-only provenance held in the spec as host_recurrence_hint and is never published; the authoring field recurrence_class records production order, not sitting order. Every count here is scoped to the sittings MIW has transcribed.

paper_status_model.available: Answers are published for this sitting.
paper_status_model.coming_later: No answers yet. Covers every case a student cannot act on -- not transcribed, in production, or source copy held only. Holding a source copy never reads as solved.

questions.verification_status: Verified as an operational and procedural answer, and honestly bounded. The fault tree, the temporary measures and the permanent measures are Chief Engineer engineering judgement grounded in the architecture of a bridge-control installation - control transmitter, remote control system, safety and interlock logic, control air, starting air, reversing arrangement and fuel. Nothing unsafe is recommended: the answer expressly forbids resetting or overriding protective trips before the cause is established. The ISM Code elements and the SOLAS chapter II-1 bridge-control requirements are referred to at the level of their well-known effect and are FLAGGED as not read in a licensed consolidated edition this session, consistent with the posture already taken on the ISM Code in Q5 of this paper. questions.question_text: Improving efficiency of propellers is recognized as a growing means to improve energy efficiency of ships. Discuss any three of the following high-efficiency propellers with its merits and demerits: a) Ducted Propellers b) Kappel Propellers c) Contra rotating Propellers. d) Azimuth Propulsion.
questions.short_title: High-Efficiency Propeller Types
questions.family_summary: Returns in the same words from March 2024 Q4.
questions.verification_status: Verified as an engineering answer, and honestly bounded. No instrument prescribes a propeller type, so ENGINEERING_JUDGEMENT is the dominant provenance class by design and this is stated rather than disguised. The hydrodynamics - the decomposition of propulsive efficiency, the axial, rotational and frictional loss mechanisms, the tip vortex, and the loading-dependence of duct benefit - are settled naval architecture and are explained mechanistically. NO PERCENTAGE EFFICIENCY GAIN IS QUOTED ANYWHERE, because published figures are vendor-sourced, hull-specific and were not verifiable. The regulatory framing that the stem supplies (ship energy efficiency) is stated WITHOUT regulation numbers, because MARPOL Annex VI was not read in a licensed consolidated edition for this question.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The hydrodynamic content of the whole answer
reverify_before_publication.why: ENGINEERING_JUDGEMENT is the sole provenance class on this question. No instrument prescribes a propeller type, so nothing here is verifiable against a regulation. The content is settled naval architecture explained mechanistically. A naval architect review before publication would be appropriate; a regulatory check would not find anything to check.

reverify_before_publication.claim: No percentage efficiency gain is quoted for any device
reverify_before_publication.why: A deliberate omission. Published gains are vendor-sourced and hull-specific. Recorded so that a later editor does not add them.

reverify_before_publication.why: MARPOL Annex VI was not read in a licensed consolidated edition for this question. If a future revision wants to cite EEXI or CII by regulation number, the Annex must be read first.

A.1208(34), adopted 3 December 2025, revoked A.1187(33) - but that is AFTER this sitting, so A.1187(33) is correct here and the successor must NOT be substituted. For any later sitting the list must be re-established, not inherited.

A.1208(34) was adopted 3 December 2025, roughly seven weeks AFTER this examination, and gathers obligations entering into force by 1 July 2026. Substituting it would import law that did not exist for the candidate. Confirm before publication that A.1187(33) still stands in this answer and has not been silently modernised.

questions.question_text: Whilst approaching dock gates, the main engines did not respond to bridge control, driving ahead instead of braking astern, until the bow made contact with the dock wall. As Chief Engineer, report to head office why the engines failed to respond to Bridge control, the temporary measure instituted to avoid further trouble on this voyage and suggesting permanent measures to avoid repetition in the future.
questions.short_title: Main Engine Failure to Respond to Bridge Control
questions.family_summary: Returns in the same words from March 2024 Q8.
questions.verification_status: Verified as an operational and procedural answer, and honestly bounded. The fault tree, the temporary measures and the permanent measures are Chief Engineer engineering judgement grounded in the architecture of a bridge-control installation - control transmitter, remote control system, safety and interlock logic, control air, starting air, reversing arrangement and fuel. Nothing unsafe is recommended: the answer expressly forbids resetting or overriding protective trips before the cause is established. The ISM Code elements and the SOLAS chapter II-1 bridge-control requirements are referred to at the level of their well-known effect and are FLAGGED as not read in a licensed consolidated edition this session, consistent with the posture already taken on the ISM Code in Q5 of this paper. No clause is quoted.

reverify_before_publication.why: The ISM Code was not read in a licensed consolidated edition this session. Confirm against a licensed edition before publication.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The SOLAS chapter II-1 bridge-control architecture - bridge control of propulsion, independent local control, and indication of shaft speed and direction
reverify_before_publication.why: SOLAS chapter II-1 was not read in a licensed consolidated edition this session. The requirement is stated in general terms with NO regulation number asserted. Confirm and add the regulation number before publication if a citation is wanted.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The fault tree, the temporary measures and the permanent measures

reverify_before_publication.claim: The answer does not diagnose a single cause
reverify_before_publication.why: Deliberate. The stem specifies neither engine type nor control architecture, so a fault tree is the correct treatment and the answer says so. Recorded so that a later editor does not "improve" it by choosing one cause.

Entry into force of the 2022 amendments on 23 December 2024 is corroborated twice and independently: the corpus instrument log, itself verified against the ILO Compendium of maritime labour instruments (4th revised edition, 2026), and the ILO's own published notice. Each of the five 2022 additions was located VERBATIM in the consolidated text and is cited to its own Standard, Guideline or Appendix rather than to 'the 2022 amendments' generally. The 2025 amendments were checked and excluded: adopted at the 113th Session in June 2025, they are not in force until an expected date in 2027, and the corpus holds them segregated so that the exclusion could be tested by term-probing the in-force text rather than argued.

questions.verification_status: The levels of ambition, indicative checkpoints and guiding principles read VERBATIM in the text of resolution MEPC.377(80); the approval of the draft new Chapter 5 at MEPC 83 and the numeric content of the framework confirmed from IMO material and a class-society source; and - the critical finding - the outcome of the second extraordinary session of MEPC in October 2025 read on the IMO's own meeting summary and press briefing, which record that the session was ADJOURNED for twelve months without adopting the amendments

reverify_before_publication.claim: That the draft new Chapter 5 of MARPOL Annex VI had been approved but NOT adopted, the extraordinary session having been adjourned for twelve months on 17 October 2025
reverify_before_publication.why: This is the single most perishable claim in the paper. The extraordinary session was due to reconvene around October 2026 - after this build. If the amendments are adopted, the entire status paragraph and every 'would' in the answer becomes wrong, while the sitting-date answer stays correct. Re-check immediately before publication and state both the sitting-date position and the current position.

reverify_before_publication.claim: The numeric content of the draft framework - GFI 93.3 baseline, ZNZ 19.0, Base and Direct Compliance Targets, USD 100 and USD 380 remedial unit prices, surplus units, the Net-Zero Fund and the 1 January 2028 first reporting period
reverify_before_publication.why: The draft Chapter 5 text was not read and no consolidated text exists because the amendments were never adopted. reverify_before_publication.claim: The procedural detail of the adjournment - Rule 31.1.2 of the MEPC Rules of Procedure and a roll call vote
reverify_before_publication.why: Taken from a class-society brief, not from the report of the session. The IMO's own summary records the adjournment and the twelve-month period but not the procedural mechanism. Confirm against the session report before publication.

questions.verification_status: Reuse of the January verified answer after a question-delta and currency review at the April sitting date, with the Code re-read at source. Confirmed again in the text of MSC.255(84): paragraph 2.22 defines a very serious marine casualty as a marine casualty involving the total loss of the ship or a death or severe damage to the environment; paragraph 2.19 defines severe damage to the environment as damage which, as evaluated by the State(s) affected or the flag State, produces a major deleterious effect upon the environment - it is an evaluative test and NOT a tonnage threshold; paragraph 2.18 defines serious injury by incapacitation for more than 72 hours commencing within seven days; chapter 6.1 requires an investigation into every very serious marine casualty; and the preamble records the flag State duties in SOLAS regulation I/21, Load Lines Article 23 and MARPOL Article 12, with SOLAS XI-1/6 making Parts I and II mandatory from 1 January 2010 by MSC.257(84).

questions.verification_status: Verified against the primary instrument, read in full. MSC-MEPC.2/Circ.12/Rev.2, Revised Guidelines for Formal Safety Assessment (FSA) for use in the IMO rule-making process, dated 9 April 2018, was obtained and read, including the purpose at 1.1.1, the terminology at section 2, the five steps at 3.1.1.1, the scope, methods and results of each step at sections 4 to 9, and appendix 7 on cost-effectiveness indices. ONE WIDELY REPEATED CLAIM WAS TESTED AND REJECTED: the Guidelines do NOT prescribe a mandatory monetary threshold for averting a fatality. Section 9.2.2 states that there are several standards for risk acceptance criteria, none as yet universally accepted, and appendix 7 states that its NCAF and GCAF values are provided for illustrative purposes only and are not static.

reverify_before_publication.claim: MSC-MEPC.2/Circ.12/Rev.2 of 9 April 2018 is the current revision of the FSA Guidelines
reverify_before_publication.why: Rev.2 was the current revision found, but this was not confirmed against an IMO circular index. The circular has been revised twice already. Confirm before publication.

reverify_before_publication.claim: No monetary criterion for averting a fatality is stated in this answer
reverify_before_publication.why: The tabulated NCAF and GCAF values in appendix 7 are presented as a table image and could not be read as text, so no figure is quoted. The claim the answer actually relies on - that the values are illustrative, not static, and must be explicitly defined by each study - was read directly in the surrounding text. If a figure is ever added it must come from the appendix itself, with its year and its illustrative status stated.
